name: Trigenys Payment Orchestrator
tagline: Give multiple applications a reliable payment interface without blurring the difference between a PSP ledger, your own accounting mirror and actual settlement.
problem: Each application integrating local and regional payment providers separately risks duplicated transactions, inconsistent webhook retries, misunderstood merchant identity and fragile settlement reporting. A shared orchestration layer needs explicit financial invariants rather than generic connector promises.
scenario: A consuming application creates a payment intent with an idempotency key. The orchestrator validates the provider's real environment/country/currency capabilities, records normalized state, verifies callback evidence and reconciles authoritative PSP records against an append-only local mirror.
differentiation: Provider capability negotiation, scoped identities, integer money amounts, deterministic replay keys and reconciliation discrepancies provide a safe shared domain model while the PSP retains custody and settlement responsibilities.
architecture: Application or TypeScript SDK -> REST v1/API core -> project and merchant context -> capability-checked provider adapters -> PSP; webhook authenticity and idempotent event receipt -> payment state and append-only ledger mirror -> reconciliation against provider source data.
limitations: The project remains a pre-production foundation/prototype; no provider is warranted as production supported. In-memory adapters and local contract tests are not durable financial settlement, certifications or live PSP enablement. Trigenys does not hold customer or merchant funds.

capabilities.name: Provider-neutral domain
capabilities.description: Represent project, merchant, payment and provider capabilities without assuming all PSP features exist.

capabilities.name: Ledger and reconciliation model
capabilities.description: Define append-only mirror semantics, discrepancy types and replay rules independent of wallet custody.

capabilities.name: Production PSP coverage
capabilities.description: Verify real credentials, country-specific capabilities and provider webhooks before committing supported rails.

capabilities.name: Durable finance operations
capabilities.description: Choose transactional persistent storage and deployment controls before handling live payment flows.

roadmap.name: Provider sandbox proof
roadmap.exitCriteria: Pass a provider-specific contract and authenticated webhook test suite with real sandbox capability evidence.

roadmap.name: Durable core
roadmap.exitCriteria: Demonstrate atomic idempotency, append-only ledger persistence, replay convergence and tenant isolation.

roadmap.name: First consumer and compliance
roadmap.exitCriteria: Complete actual consumer integration, threat review and regulatory evaluation before enabling live payments.
